answer: For a Share Certificate with a term longer than 12 months, the early withdrawal penalty is 180 days of dividends (terms of 12 months or less are 90 days). This is under the Share Certificate Account Disclosure, version DEP-DSC-017. The penalty is calculated on the amount withdrawn at the dividend rate in effect on the certificate, and it can reduce your principal if the dividends earned are less than the penalty. Note that early withdrawals of principal are only allowed as a full withdrawal. The penalty is waived if an owner dies or is declared legally incompetent by a court, and you also have a 10-day grace period after maturity to withdraw without penalty.

Mobile and Online Banking Help

Use this page to get started with Harbor online banking and the Harbor mobile app, and to troubleshoot common issues.

Signing In

I forgot my password. What should I do?

Select Forgot Password on the sign-in screen. We will send a one-time passcode to the phone number or e-mail address on file. Your new password must be at least 12 characters and cannot match any of your last five passwords.

Why is my access locked?

After five (5) consecutive failed sign-in attempts your access is locked for 30 minutes. After the lockout period you can try again, or reset your password immediately using Forgot Password. If you did not attempt to sign in, contact us, because someone else may be trying to access your account.

Can I use fingerprint or face recognition?

Yes. After you sign in with your password once on a device, go to Settings and turn on biometric sign-in. Biometric sign-in is tied to the device, so you will need to enable it again on a new phone.

Here's how a card dispute works under the Card Dispute Procedure, Rev 5 (effective 15 April 2026):

1. Form: The agent completes Form HCU-DSP-114 (Card Transaction Dispute) during your first contact, whether by phone, in branch or secure message. It records the transaction date, amount, merchant descriptor, your explanation, and whether you still have the card. The agent verifies you with the three-factor authentication script, confirms the transaction, blocks and replaces the card if fraud is suspected, reads the dispute acknowledgment disclosure, and routes the case to the Card Services dispute queue. Disputes should be reported within 60 days of the statement date on which the transaction first appeared; later reports are still logged but liability protections and the right to provisional credit may be limited.

2. Provisional credit: Posted within 10 business days of receiving the dispute notice if the investigation isn't finished by then, or within 20 business days if the account was opened less than 30 days before the first disputed transaction. You're notified of the amount and date within 2 business days of posting. For credit card disputes, no provisional credit is given; instead the disputed amount is suspended from the balance and excluded from finance charges while the investigation is open.

3. Investigation length: Must be completed within 45 calendar days of receiving the dispute notice, extended to 90 calendar days for point-of-sale transactions, foreign-initiated transactions, and transactions on accounts opened in the previous 30 days. Any chargeback is submitted to the network no later than 120 calendar days after the transaction settlement date.

4. Outcome notice: Card Services writes to you within 3 business days of completing the investigation. If the dispute is decided in your favour, any provisional credit becomes final. If Harbor finds no error occurred, the notice explains the findings, your right to request the documents relied upon, and the date provisional credit will be reversed \u2014 at least 5 business days after the notice is sent.

Under Harbor's Account Closure Procedure v1.4 (MS-PRO-012, effective June 1, 2026), closing a retail share or checking account works like this:

Before starting: the request must come from an account owner, and on joint accounts every owner must consent. We'll review linked services that will fail (direct deposits, automatic loan payments, bill pay payees, P2P enrollments) so you can redirect them. Note that closing the Primary Share Account ends membership, and it can't be closed while you have an open loan 
inch it must be paid in full first.

Steps:
1. Identity verification 
sic two forms of ID in branch, or the three-factor authentication script by phone.
2. A signed Form HCU-ACL-220 (Account Closure Request) from every owner.
3. Review of pending items, holds and scheduled transfers, noted on the form.
4. Cancel debit cards, stop recurring transfers, remove bill pay payees.
5. Account moved to Closing status and disbursement method recorded.
6. Deposit Operations completes the pending items review.
7. Remaining balance disbursed and account set to Closed.
8. Closure confirmation letter sent; form retained in the member file.

Timelines: phone requests are accepted only for single-owner accounts, and the signed form must be returned by mail or secure upload before step 5. After the pending-items review period, the balance is disbursed by official check mailed within 7 business days to the address on file; alternatively it can be transferred to another Harbor member's account with their consent, or paid in cash in branch if the balance is under $2,500. Dividends are paid through the date of closure. If the account is overdrawn, the closure is not completed 
sic it's referred under the Overdraft Policy with a recovery case. The form and confirmation letter are kept for five years after closure.

One part I can't confirm from the material I have: the exact length of the pending-items review period in Section 4.

1. Purpose

This procedure explains how Member Service Representatives (MSRs) and Member Contact Centre agents close Retail share and checking accounts at a member's request, and how remaining funds are returned. It does not cover closures initiated by Harbor for risk or policy reasons, which follow the Involuntary Closure Standard.

citations.text:
Account Closure Procedure
2. Before You Begin

Confirm that the request comes from an owner of the account. For joint accounts, every owner must consent to the closure. Review the account for linked services that will fail once the account is closed, including direct deposits, automatic loan payments, bill pay payees, and person-to-person payment enrollments, and explain to the member which services they need to redirect.

Closing the Primary Share Account ends the member's membership. If the member has an open loan, the Primary Share Account cannot be closed until the loan is paid in full.
citations.title: Account Closure Procedure

citations.text:
Account Closure Procedure
3. Closure Steps

Step | Action | Owner
1 | Verify the member's identity using two forms of identification in branch or the three-factor authentication script by phone. | MSR or agent
2 | Obtain a signed Form HCU-ACL-220 (Account Closure Request) from every owner on the account. | MSR
3 | Review pending items, holds and scheduled transfers in the core system and note them on the form. | MSR
4 | Cancel debit cards, stop recurring transfers and remove bill pay payees linked to the account. | MSR
5 | Move the account to Closing status and record the requested disbursement method. | MSR
6 | Complete the pending items review described in Section 4. | Deposit Operations
7 | Disburse the remaining balance as described in Section 5 and set the account to Closed. | Deposit Operations
8 | Send the closure confirmation letter and retain the form in the member file. | Deposit Operations

Phone requests may be accepted for single-owner accounts only, and the signed form must be returned by mail or secure upload before step 5 can be completed.
citations.title: Account Closure Procedure

citations.text:
Account Closure Procedure
5. Disbursement of Remaining Funds

After the review period, the remaining balance is disbursed by official check mailed within 7 business days to the address on file. At the member's request, funds may instead be transferred to another Harbor member's account with that member's consent, or paid out in cash in branch if the balance is under $2,500. Dividends are paid through the date of closure.

If the account is overdrawn at closure, do not complete the closure. Refer the member to the Overdraft Policy and create a recovery case.
citations.title: Account Closure Procedure

citations.text:
Account Closure Procedure
7. Records

Form HCU-ACL-220 and the closure confirmation letter are retained for five years after closure. Closed accounts are reported to the account screening agency only where the account was closed with a negative balance.

2. Intake and Timeframes

Members must report an unauthorized or disputed card transaction within 60 days of the statement date on which the transaction first appeared. Disputes received after this period are still logged, but Harbor's liability protections and the member's right to provisional credit may be limited.

2. Confirm the transaction details against the card processing system.

3. If fraud is suspected, block the card immediately and order a replacement.

4. Complete Form HCU-DSP-114 and read the dispute acknowledgment disclosure.

5. Route the case to the Card Services dispute queue in the case management system.

Under the Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy v1.6, your consumer loan payment is treated as late only if it isn't received within 15 calendar days after the due date on your billing statement. Payments made within that grace period count as on-time for fee purposes (though interest keeps accruing daily on simple-interest loans until payment arrives). If the last day of the grace period falls on a weekend or Federal Reserve holiday, it extends to the next business day.

The late fee is 5% of the scheduled payment amount or $25.00, whichever is less. Only one late fee is charged per scheduled payment, and you're never charged a new late fee just because an earlier one is unpaid. No late fees apply while you're meeting the terms of an approved hardship program.

This covers closed-end consumer loans (new/used auto, personal and share-secured loans); credit cards, HELOCs and first mortgages have their own agreements.

question: What is the daily point-of-sale purchase limit on a Harbor debit card?
reply:
Your Harbor debit card has a standard daily point-of-sale purchase limit of $3,000, covering purchases in stores, online and by phone (Debit Card Limits and Controls, effective 2026-02-02, for Harbor Visa debit cards on Retail checking accounts). Premier Checking cardholders may have higher limits — you can see your current limits in the Harbor app under Card Controls — Limits.
